canonical.title: The React state stack for Itenium.Forge in 2026: the Redux question dissolves

children.title: Generating the itenium-ui API client from Forge's OpenAPI document
children.summary: Orval is the pick for itenium-ui: it is the only generator that emits TanStack Query hooks, query keys, MSW mocks and Zod schemas from one config — and generating the client collapses the state-management question to 'server cache + a little client state'.

children.title: Server-state layer for a React 19 + Vite SPA on a .NET API: TanStack Query wins
children.summary: TanStack Query is the correct server-state layer for itenium-ui; its Register.defaultError hook makes RFC 9457 ProblemDetails a first-class typed error with no per-call generics.

children.title: The router is a state manager: TanStack Router for itenium-ui
children.summary: For itenium-ui — a greenfield React 19 + Vite SPA with no SSR — pick TanStack Router: it is the only option that makes filters/sort/pagination typed URL state instead of Redux slices, and it composes with TanStack Query rather than competing.

children.title: Client state after the query cache: Zustand vs Jotai vs RTK vs plain React 19
children.summary: Once TanStack Query owns server state, the residual client state in a CRUD admin is roughly one persisted preferences store — take Zustand's vanilla createStore in a shared Nx lib and skip the rest.

children.title: Auth & session state for a React 19 SPA on Forge: kill the localStorage plan
children.summary: Drop the localStorage JWT plan: use react-oidc-context with an in-memory access token, put roles/capabilities behind a /me query instead of in the token, and treat a .NET BFF as the target end-state.

children.title: Is Redux still the right answer for a new React 19 app in 2026?
children.summary: Redux is healthy but no longer the default: for a greenfield React 19 SPA talking to a REST API, TanStack Query plus a small Zustand store wins, and Redux's classic moats — devtools, time-travel, testable reducers — no longer belong to Redux alone.

sources.title: Redux FAQ: General
sources.claim: Redux's own FAQ says not all apps need Redux and quotes Dan Abramov advising not to use Redux until you have problems with vanilla React.

sources.title: TanStack Query — Does this replace client state?
sources.claim: Once async code moves to TanStack Query, the remaining truly-global client state is usually tiny — typically just themeMode and sidebarStatus.

sources.title: TanStack Router — External data loading
sources.claim: Route loaders and TanStack Query compose rather than compete: the loader calls ensureQueryData() and the component reads the same cache via useSuspenseQuery().

sources.claim: Zustand v5 uses useSyncExternalStore semantics: an object-returning selector loops forever unless wrapped in useShallow.

sources.title: Duende — the BFF pattern
sources.claim: In the BFF pattern the SPA holds only an httpOnly SameSite session cookie plus a CSRF header; tokens never reach the browser.

sources.title: TanStack Query — Query invalidation
sources.claim: invalidateQueries supports prefix matching by default, exact: true, and an arbitrary predicate.

sources.title: Nx — configure task outputs
sources.claim: Nx caches a target's declared outputs, so an OpenAPI codegen target can be cached on its inputs.

sources.title: RTK Query vs TanStack Query
sources.claim: TanStack Query replaces the server-state portion of Redux, which is 60-80% of Redux code in data-driven apps.

sources.title: TanStack/query discussion #3653
sources.claim: Combining a 401-retry interceptor with TanStack Query's retry logic causes duplicate refresh attempts; auth failures should be handled once centrally.
